text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn announced Sunday that as a result of the Tocsik scandal he would move to have Minister of Industry and Trade Tamas Suchman relieved of his post. The cabinet decided on Friday to dismiss the entire management of the State Privatisation and Holding Co.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin has arrived in Budapest on an official visit.
- The Alliance of Free Democrats will hold a convention of delegates on November 22-23. @
- The opposition Hungarian Democratic Forum staged a demonstration outside Parliament on Saturday.
- The construction of Terminal 2B of Budapest's Ferihegy Airport is to begin in early December. The project will cost approximately $120 million.
- The Finnish-Japanese consortium IVO-Tomen bought a 73.7 percent stake in Budapest Power Station for $47 million Thursday. (Sat.)
- The Austrian bank GiroCredit Bank AG is to submit a bid for a stake in Takarekbank, said managing director Ferdinand Lacina. @
- Alfa TV, the brainchild of Czech film director Jiri Menzel, chairman of the First Central and East European Cooperation Foundation, has announced that Budapest will be the headquarters of Alfa TV.
- Police and the civil secret services launched a large-scale investigation into an explosion at Piliscsaba on a regional bus possibly caused by nitroglycerin.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Hungary has been admitted to the Nuclear Energy Agency. @
- Hungary already provides all the economic data required by the IMF's new data reporting standards, said IMF coordinator in Hungary Gyorgy Szilagyi.
- Electricity prices should be raised by 20-30 percent from January, said Imre Szabo, head of the Hungarian Energy Office.
- DEM 120 milion of a DEM 1 billion German loan is to be spent on the modernisation of the 19.5 km Hungarian stretch of the railway line connecting Hungary and Slovenia.
NEPSZAVA
- Portuguese Defence Minister Antonio Vitorino is due to arrive in Budapest today. @
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The government has submitted a supplementary budget for social insurance funds to cover this year.
- The 13 insurance companies operating in Hungary paid out a total of HUF 3.8 billion for damages in the first half of this year, 30 per cent more than in the same period of last year.
- A 94.91 percent stake of HUF 4.1 billion face value in Forum Hotel Rt. has been purchased by the Intercontinental Hotel Co. for $49.4 million.
NEPSZABADSAG @

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said in an interview to the German daily Suddeutsche Zeitung that living conditions will not drop any further from 1997, and an improvement may begin based on well-founded economic growth in the coming years.
